A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same TaRoS research, with readable text, equations, figures, and tables. However, both end at References without the supplementary material cited in the text, limiting comparison of supplement-only analyses and implementation details.

before.justification: v2 reports original VBench experiments, reward analyses, ablations, and a user study involving 65 raters evaluating 20 video pairs each.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results, reward analyses, ablations, and user-study outcomes in Tables 1–6 and the accompanying figures.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same component utilities based on group means and Hoyer sparsity, softmax reward weighting, aggregated rewards, standardized advantages, and clipped GRPO objective. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both retain the DanceGRPO 50k training dataset, iStock ablation and reward-analysis data, VBench evaluation, and text-to-video and human-comparison tasks. Removing metric rows does not establish reduced evaluation coverage; Section 5.1 still specifies sixteen VBench dimensions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: Wan1.3B and DanceGRPO variants in Table 1, Wan14B in Table 2, HunyuanVideo in Table 3, and the two- and three-component DanceGRPO variants in Table 4. The reward-model comparisons also retain the same participants.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes Wan1.3B training clips from 53 frames at 15 fps to 81 frames at 16 fps. Wan14B training and inference for both Wan models change from 15 to 16 fps. Splits, learning rates, group sizes, and training-step counts remain unchanged. These are reported setting revisions; neither PDF establishes that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The displayed component-count ablation, threshold and beta sensitivity results, reward analyses, and qualitative cases remain unchanged. v3 deletes v2's reference to additional supplementary reward curves testing hyperparameter sensitivity. Those curves are absent from both supplied PDFs, so an actual analysis removal cannot be distinguished from deletion of its textual pointer.

E5.justification: The coefficient-of-variation analysis and reward-standard-deviation plots retain the same reporting practices. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 each remove seven metric rows: background consistency, color, dynamic degree, motion smoothness, subject consistency, temporal flickering, and temporal style. This removes 63 scores and substantially narrows the reported evidence about temporal behavior and quality tradeoffs across both Wan backbones. These entries are not relocated elsewhere in the supplied PDFs. Retained scores, Tables 3–6, and plotted findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The ODE/SDE preliminaries and TaRoS mathematical definitions and objectives in Equations 1–11 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or removed in the supplied material.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same two diagnosed reward failures, TaRoS contribution, and claims of improved stability, visual quality, motion coherence, and alignment. The added sample-efficiency future-work sentence introduces no new contribution claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of shortcut optimization, saturation, evaluator bias, and visual-first optimization remain unchanged. The qualification that TaRoS mitigates rather than completely eliminates reward hacking is retained. The new future-work sentence supplies no substantive limitation or mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 changes reported H100 counts from 8 to 16 for Wan1.3B and from 16 to 32 for both Wan14B and HunyuanVideo. It also removes pointers to supplementary Qwen scoring templates, threshold-computation rules, and further implementation details. The referenced template and detailed rules are not supplied in either PDF.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Qwen2.5-VL technical report and Exposure Bias Can Alleviate Itself via Directional and Frequency Rectification in Flow Matching. It removes LIV and redirects the VideoAlign citation to the already cited Improving Video Generation with Human Feedback. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises author and affiliation information, adds contribution and correspondence markers, corrects several spelling and table-label errors, removes supplementary pointers, and adds one future-work sentence. Section order and the main narrative are preserved.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 are shortened by deleting metric rows. Table 3 and Figures 5–6 move earlier as the document reflows. All six figures are retained with the same substantive visual content; the remaining tables undergo only limited labeling or placement changes.

improvement.justification: v3 provides less complete evidence for its unchanged broad performance claims. The omitted motion and temporal metrics in Tables 1–2 exposed mixed outcomes in v2, while Section 5.3 still discusses the removed color and background-consistency results. Small editorial and citation improvements do not offset this loss of evidential transparency, although the method and most experiments remain intact.
